title: Kubernetes WAS v1alpha3 improvements (in-place gang resize + PodGroupPremptionPolicy)
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

This PR implements Kubernetes Workload Aware Scheduling added to the `v1alpha3` scheduling API in Kubernetes v1.37.

New functionality includes:
- Support for ray cluster autoscaling (which is now possible because PodGroup.minCount is mutable)
- PodGroupPremptionPolicy (can specify if a PodGroup can be pre-empted by workloads with a higher PriorityClass)

## Related issue number

Part of https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/4344

## Labels

<!-- Please add the appropriate labels to this PR. -->

- [x] If this PR has user-facing changes that require documentation updates at release time, I have added the `doc-updates-required` label.
- [ ] If this PR contains breaking changes, I have added the `breaking-change` label.

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
  - [x] Unit tests
  - [x] Manual tests
  - [ ] This PR is not tested :(

<!-- If you selected "Manual tests" above, please fill in the section below. Otherwise you can remove it. -->

### Manual test instructions

1. Start a kind cluster with required feature gates

```bash
kind create cluster --name k8s-was --config ray-operator/hack/kind-config-kubernetes-was-v1alpha3.yml
```

2. Build, load, deploy kuberay operator

```bash
cd ray-operator
IMG=kuberay/operator:v1alpha3-was make docker-image
IMG=kuberay/operator:v1alpha3-was make deploy-kubernetes-was-v1alpha3
kubectl wait --for=condition=Available=true deployment/kuberay-operator --timeout=120s
```

3. Create a `Never` PriorityClass

```bash
kubecrtl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiversion: scheduling.k9s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: { name: ray-no-premption }
value: 1000
premptionPolicy:NEVER
EOF
```

4. Deploy a gang-scheduling-enabled ray cluster - start with something like `ray-operator/config/samples/ray-cluster.sample.yaml, **name it was-demo.yaml**, and add the following label and  ProirtyClass to **the head and worker** pod templates, and apply it

```yaml
metadata:
  name: was-demo
  labels: { ray.io/gang-scheduling-enabled: "true" }
spec:
  headGroupSpec:
    template: { spec:  { priorityClassName: ray-no-premption } }
  workerGroupSpecs:
    - replicas: 2
      minReplicas: 2
      template: { spec: { priorityClassName: ray-no-premption }}
```

```bash
kubectl apply -f was-demo.yaml
kubectl wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.state}'=ready raycluster/was-demo
```

5. inspect the workload and podgroup objects

```bash
 kubectl get workload,podgroup
 kubectl get pods -l ray.io/cluster=was-demo -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GROUP:.spec.schedulingGroup.podGroupName
 ```

6. inspect the pod group's premption policy

```bash
kubectl get podgroup was-demo-cluster -o jsonpath='{.spec.priorityClassName}{" -> "}{.spec.preemptionPolicy}{"\n"}'
kubectl get workload was-demo -o jsonpath='{.spec.podGroupTemplates[0].preemptionPolicy}{"\n"}'
```

7. in-place resize the worker group

```bash
kubectl get podgroup was-demo-cluster -o jsonpath='UID={.metadata.uid} minCount={.spec.schedulingPolicy.gang.minCount}{"\n"}'
kubectl patch raycluster was-demo --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/workerGroupSpecs/0/replicas","value":3}]'
   # expect minCount=4 (1 head + 3 workers), same UID
kubectl get podgroup was-demo-cluster -o jsonpath='UID={.metadata.uid} minCount={.spec.schedulingPolicy.gang.minCount}{"\n"}'
```

title: [Dashboard] Resolve the Ray head dashboard link by Service port name
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

The dashboard resolved the Ray head dashboard port by scanning the head group spec for a container port literally named `dashboard`, and returned an empty link when it was absent (`useListClusters.ts`, `useListJobs.ts`). The link then just vanished from the row with no explanation — even though the dashboard was still reachable.

That named port is optional. When the head container declares no ports at all — which is the case for several samples under `ray-operator/config/samples/` and for `historyserver/config/raycluster.yaml` — the operator falls back to the default ports when it builds the head Service:

- `getServicePorts` ([`ray-operator/controllers/ray/common/service.go`](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/blob/master/ray-operator/controllers/ray/common/service.go)) uses `getDefaultPorts()`, which includes `dashboard: 8265`, whenever the head container declares no ports.
- `updateStatus` ([`ray-operator/controllers/ray/raycluster_controller.go`](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/blob/master/ray-operator/controllers/ray/raycluster_controller.go)) then copies the head Service ports into `status.endpoints`, keyed by port name.

So the dashboard port exists on the Service; the spec just doesn't mention it.

This PR builds the link from the Service port **name** instead of a container port number — the Service proxy subresource accepts `services/<head-svc>:dashboard/proxy/` — and decides whether to show the link from `status.endpoints`. Only the *presence* of the `dashboard` key there is usable: its value is the nodePort or targetPort, not the Service port, so it can't be substituted into the URL.

The logic is shared between the two hooks by a new `buildRayHeadDashboardLink` helper in `dashboard/src/utils/links.ts`.

Behavior change: clusters/jobs whose head container omits the named `dashboard` port now show a working dashboard link. Clusters whose head Service genuinely has no `dashboard` port still show no link, as before.

Closes #5179

### Manual test instructions

```bash

kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'

kind: RayCluster
metadata:
  name: rc-noports
spec:
```

title: [ray-operator] Add spec.idleSuspend and spec.idleTerminationOptions for v1 RayCluster CRD
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->
 
## Why are these changes needed?

<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

The Ray Autoscaler can scale worker pods down to zero based on idleTimeoutSeconds, but the RayCluster custom resource and its associated resources still remain in the cluster. As a result, the head pod continues to consume resources and may reserve capacity even when the cluster is otherwise idle. Users who do not want to retain the head pod or its reserved capacity must manually delete the RayCluster. 

With https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65763, the Ray Autoscaler automatically terminates an idle RayCluster when it has no attached user driver. This PR aims to implement KubeRay's side of the [idle termination](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GFdgyfrHBfI-UNlaGgnVDMcx9-K9Eawjg2LW4GVTjRI/) feature by introducing two apis, which are `idleSuspend` and `idleTerminationOptions`. 

When `idleTerminationOptions` is set, the ray autoscaler will terminate an idle RayCluster. If the idleTerminationOptions.policy is Suspend, the ray autoscaler will patch idleSuspend=true, and the reconcile loop will recognize it and suspend the cluster same as how spec.Suspend works. The only difference is the reason emit in the event. 

On the other hand, when idleTerminationOptions.policy is Delete, the reconcile loop will log the event and remove the finalizer to allow the deletion.

## Changes:

### API and Constants
- Add IdleSuspend to RayClusterSpec.
- Add `TimeoutSeconds` and `Policy` to `IdleTerminationOptions`.
- Add the `ray.io/no-driver-idle-termination` finalizer and `RayClusterIdleSuspended` condition reason.

### Reconciliation 
- Treat `IdleSuspend`  as a suspension trigger and reuse the existing RayCluster suspend flow.
- Set `RayClusterIdleSuspended` as the condition reason when suspension is triggered by idle termination.
- Handle the idle-termination finalizer during deletion and remove it after recording the corresponding logs and events. Once removed, let it fall through without returning so that other finalizers can addressed. 

### RBAC 
- Grant the autoscaler delete permission only for the target RayCluster using resourceNames. 

### Validation and Compatibility
- Require Autoscaler v2 and enableInTreeAutoscaling when `IdleTerminationOptions.TimeoutSeconds` is configured.
- Validate the timeout and policy configuration.
- Exclude RayJob, RayService, Ray versions earlier than 2.56.
(**will be bumped to 2.59.0 once https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65763 is merged**)
 
## Related issue number

Closes https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/2998

Ray https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65763

## Why are these changes needed?

The API server returns `serviceAccount`, but the Python client's head and worker decoders read `service_account`, losing the configured account. The head serializer also writes `image_pull_secret` while its decoder reads `imagePullSecret`, losing the pull secret in a round trip.

Use the API's camelCase field names for serialization and decoding, while continuing to accept keys emitted by earlier client versions. Add regression coverage for both node types and legacy payloads.

title: python-client: allow zero worker replicas
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

The Python client checks worker-group replica counts by truthiness. As a result, `ClusterBuilder.build_worker(replicas=0)` cannot build a worker group, and `ClusterUtils.update_worker_group_replicas(..., replicas=0, min_replicas=0)` returns `False` instead of scaling an existing group down to zero. title: Support custom resource configuration for the submit pod
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

This PR introduces support for customizing resource requests and limits for the submit pod.

1. In CPU-constrained clusters, users may wish to reduce the submit pod's CPU request (e.g., to 400m) to avoid scheduling delays or resource exhaustion. Previously, adjusting submit pod resources required modifying the codebase and rebuilding the binary, which was inconvenient and error-prone.

2. For large-scale clusters with high task throughput, the ability to configure submit pod resources dynamically is essential for stability and operational flexibility.

3. The community-provided default `submitterTemplate` requires users to fully override the entire pod spec — including image name, startup arguments, and other fields — even when they only want to change the resource settings. This is unnecessarily complex for most use cases where only minor adjustments to resource limits are needed.

This enhancement provides a cleaner and more configurable approach to submit pod resource tuning.

We can use the rayjob like 

```
apiVersion: ray.io/v1
kind: RayJob
metadata:
  name: rayjob-sample
spec:
  submitterConfig:
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "250m"
        memory: "256Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "500m"
        memory: "512Mi"
  runtimeEnvYAML: |
    pip:
      - requests==2.26.0
      - pendulum==2.1.2
    env_vars:
      counter_name: "test_counter"

  rayClusterSpec:
    rayVersion: '2.41.0' # should match the Ray version in the image of the containers
    # Ray head pod template
    headGroupSpec:
      # The `rayStartParams` are used to configure the `ray start` command.
      # See https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/blob/master/docs/guidance/rayStartParams.md for the default settings of `rayStartParams` in KubeRay.
      # See https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/cli.html#ray-start for all available options in `rayStartParams`.
      rayStartParams: {}
      #pod template
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: ray-head
              image: harbor.weizhipin.com/arsenal-oceanus/ray:2.41.0
              ports:
                - containerPort: 6379
                  name: gcs-server
                - containerPort: 8265 # Ray dashboard
                  name: dashboard
                - containerPort: 10001
                  name: client
              resources:
                limits:
                  cpu: "1"
                requests:
                  cpu: "200m"
              volumeMounts:
                - mountPath: /home/ray/samples
                  name: code-sample
          volumes:
            # You set volumes at the Pod level, then mount them into containers inside that Pod
            - name: code-sample
              configMap:
                # Provide the name of the ConfigMap you want to mount.
                name: ray-job-code-sample
                # An array of keys from the ConfigMap to create as files
                items:
                  - key: sample_code.py
                    path: sample_code.py
    workerGroupSpecs:
      # the pod replicas in this group typed worker
      - replicas: 1
        minReplicas: 1
        maxReplicas: 5
        # logical group name, for this called small-group, also can be functional
        groupName: small-group
        rayStartParams: {}
        #pod template
        template:
          spec:
            containers:
              - name: ray-worker # must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'my-name',  or '123-abc'
                image: harbor.weizhipin.com/arsenal-oceanus/ray:2.41.0
                resources:
                  limits:
                    cpu: "1"
                  requests:
                    cpu: "200m"

######################Ray code sample#################################
# this sample is from https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/cluster/job-submission.html#quick-start-example
# it is mounted into the container and executed to show the Ray job at work
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: ray-job-code-sample
data:
  sample_code.py: |
    import ray
    import os
    import requests

    ray.init()

    @ray.remote
    class Counter:
        def __init__(self):
            # Used to verify runtimeEnv
            self.name = os.getenv("counter_name")
            assert self.name == "test_counter"
            self.counter = 0

        def inc(self):
            self.counter += 1

        def get_counter(self):
            return "{} got {}".format(self.name, self.counter)

    counter = Counter.remote()

    for _ in range(5):
        ray.get(counter.inc.remote())
        print(ray.get(counter.get_counter.remote()))

    # Verify that the correct runtime env was used for the job.
    assert requests.__version__ == "2.26.0"
```

## Checks

- [✅ ] I've made sure the tests are passing.

In the current setup of dependabot, if k8s modules get updated in one component, other componets may be afftected which causing check fails. 7. cd ./ray-operator && ./hack/update-codegen.sh
8. cd ./ray-operator && make manifests && make sync
9. cd ./apiserver && make generate

After catching up, those change will be submitted as a new commit by Dependabot

title: [Fix] Unmask CI failures and fix ready-endpoints check in TestZeroDowntimeUpgradeAfterOperatorUpgrade
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

This PR addresses two issues in the operator upgrade e2e test suite:

### 1. Fix masked test failures in CI script (`test-e2e.yml`)
* **Problem:** The test command piped `go test` output without `set -o pipefail`, causing the pipeline to evaluate only the final command's exit code and allowing test failures to be reported as green.
* **Fix:** Added `set -o pipefail` to ensure test execution failures properly fail the CI job.

### 2. Configure Ray Serve replica distribution for zero-downtime upgrade
* **Problem:** In `TestZeroDowntimeUpgradeAfterOperatorUpgrade`, the RayService deployment used `num_replicas: 1`. Without distributing replicas across multiple worker nodes, the service could not maintain high availability or produce the expected ready endpoints across distinct nodes during rolling upgrades.
* **Fix:** Updated the Serve application configuration to set `num_replicas: 2` and `max_replicas_per_node: 1`. This forces Ray Serve to schedule replicas onto separate worker nodes, ensuring continuous endpoint availability and true zero downtime during upgrades.

## Related issue number

Closes #5317

## Why are these changes needed?
This is an example of setting up gRPC on KubeRay, and this example is consistent with [that on Ray Serve](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/serve/advanced-guides/grpc-guide.html#send-grpc-requests-to-serve-deployments).

The following are the steps:

1. Use the command `python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I./protos --python_out=. --pyi_out=. --grpc_python_out=. ./protos/user_defined_protos.proto`  which is provided in the proto file to generate the Python code.
This command would generate three files, including `user_defined_protos_pb2.py`, `user_defined_protos_pb2.pyi`, `user_defined_protos_pb2_grpc.py`.

2. Use the YAML file `ray-serve-grpc.yaml` to create the RayService CR.

title: when running ray start, getting resources value from environment variables
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?
In a ray cluster, getting the resources value from the environment variable when launching a ray cluster. 

Currently the ray start command is as below, 
`ulimit -n 65536; ray start --head  --num-cpus=8  --memory=68719476736  --num-gpus=2 .....`
The number of resources (cpu/memory/gpu) are from the rayStartParams in the crd. If any of them is not specified, it will get the value from resources.limits[$resourceName] of the container. The "ray start ...." command is generated by the ray operator, which means we have to set the resources value of the ray cluster before the pods for raycluster are created. It is unable to update the resources dynamically.

The change of this PR is to get the resources from the environment variable if the resources in rayStartParams are not set so the value of the resources can be changed after the pod for the ray cluster are created. 
<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->
This PR includes the following changes,
1. Creating environment variables RAY_NUM_CPUS, RAY_MEMORY, RAY_NUM_GPUS.
2. If any of the resources is not set in rayStartParams, the "ray start" cmd will get the value from environment variables, e.g. if we don't set the value of num_cpus in rayStartParams but set memory and num-gpus, the generated cmd will be like `ulimit -n 65536; ray start --head  --num-cpus=$RAY_NUM_CPUS  --memory=68719476736  --num-gpus=2 .....`
3.  To make it backward compatitble, the default value of these environment variable will be the resources.limit[$resourceName]  respectively.

title: fix(raycluster): stop recreate loop on YuniKorn ResourceReservationTimeout
body:
## Fixes

Fixes #5301

## Summary

When YuniKorn hard-gang `placeholderTimeoutInSeconds` expires, Pods are failed with `Reason: ResourceReservationTimeout` and the YuniKorn application is removed. KubeRay previously treated those as ordinary terminal Pods, deleted them, and recreated replacements against the same dead `applicationId`, leaving RayJob running until `activeDeadlineSeconds`.

This change:

1. Treats `Failed` + `ResourceReservationTimeout` as a non-recreate terminal failure in `shouldDeletePod`.
2. Short-circuits `reconcilePods` when such Pods are present (or when `Status.Reason` is already set) so `WorkersToDelete` cannot remove them and trigger recreation.
3. Surfaces the failure on RayCluster (`Status.State=failed`, `Status.Reason=ResourceReservationTimeout`, and `BatchSchedulingFailed` condition when the status-conditions feature gate is enabled).
4. Transitions RayJob to `Failed` with `Reason=ResourceReservationTimeout` while waiting for the cluster to become ready.

A broader `BatchScheduler` plugin hook (issue option 3) is left for a follow-up / maintainer design choice; this implements the smallest correct stop-recreate + surface-failure path.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `shouldDeletePod` with `Failed` + `ResourceReservationTimeout`
- [x] Fake-client reconcilePods test: RRT Pods are not deleted/recreated; Status.Reason short-circuit skips recreation after Pods are gone

title: [RayJob] Don't fail a running Ray job when the submitter exits
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

KubeRay treats the submitter finishing as evidence the Ray job is terminal. It isn't. `ray job logs --follow`, the submitter's last command in `K8sJobMode` and `SidecarMode`, returns **0** on any non-abnormal WebSocket close ([sdk.py](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/master/python/ray/dashboard/modules/job/sdk.py)):

```python
elif msg.type == aiohttp.WSMsgType.CLOSED:
    if ws.close_code == aiohttp.WSCloseCode.ABNORMAL_CLOSURE:
        raise RuntimeError(...)
    break                                  # normal close: no error
...
return _log_job_status(client, job_id)     # only logs; never exits non-zero
```

`checkSubmitterFinishedTimeoutAndUpdateStatusIfNeeded` then waits 30s, overwrites `RUNNING` with `FAILED`, and under `shutdownAfterJobFinishes` deletes the cluster from under the driver. It also produces the inconsistent status pair in #2314.

### Ask the cluster instead of guessing

The timeout can't just be removed: #4091 added it for a status that never resolves after a head restart. Both cases arrive with `JobStatus: RUNNING`.

A job status is only current while the node running its driver is alive. Ray already reports `driver_node_id` on the job; this deserializes it and adds an `IsNodeAlive` check against the dashboard's node list:

```go
if rayJobIsActive(rayJob) {
    alive, err := rayJobDriverIsAlive(ctx, dashboardClient, jobInfo)
    ...
    if alive { return false, nil }   // job is genuinely running; leave it
}
```

The check moves after the job-info poll, where `jobInfo` and the client are already available. It compares no timestamps and reads no Pod lifecycle, so it is unaffected by readiness probes flapping, by a sidecar submitter dying, and by whether the head restarted before or after the submitter exited, earlier revisions got each of those wrong, and Bugbot caught them.

Scoped to `RUNNING` on purpose: Ray assigns `driver_node_id` when it schedules the job's supervisor, so a `PENDING` job has none to check against. Those keep today's behavior rather than being guessed at. An unreachable dashboard returns an error and requeues instead of counting as a dead driver, and a `jobInfo` that has already gone terminal is left to the normal handling.

The e2e test `RayJob has exceed SubmitterFinishedTimeout` asserted the old behaviour; it is rewritten to assert the job survives, and renamed.

## Related issue number

Addresses #4921. Related: #2314.

## Labels

- [ ] `doc-updates-required`
- [ ] `breaking-change`

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
  - [x] Unit tests
  - [x] Manual tests

### Manual test instructions

kind, `rayproject/ray:2.55.1`, `shutdownAfterJobFinishes: false` so the cluster survives for inspection.

Repro: SIGTERM the head's dashboard `JobHead` module mid-job. That ends the submitter's `ray job logs --follow` stream without touching the raylet, so the node stays up and the job keeps running.

**On unpatched `master` — a healthy job is failed.**

```
[07:03:09Z] SIGTERM JobHead
[07:03:25Z] submitter=Succeeded/0 | js=RUNNING dep=Running
[07:03:55Z] submitter=Succeeded/0 | js=FAILED  dep=Failed
            reason=JobDeploymentStatusTransitionGracePeriodExceeded
```

Ray's own view at that moment, while the CR said `FAILED`:

```
node 01c291fbf6981517 state=ALIVE
ray job status = RUNNING   driver_node = 01c291fbf6981517
entrypoint process: still running
```

It then ran to completion, four minutes after KubeRay gave up on it:

```
[07:04:37Z] ray=RUNNING     CR=FAILED
[07:08:02Z] ray=SUCCEEDED   CR=FAILED
```

With `shutdownAfterJobFinishes` on, the cluster is deleted at 07:03:55 and that work is lost.

**On this branch — same repro, job survives.**

```
[06:55:11Z] submitter finished
[06:55:41Z] "The RayJob submitter finished but the Ray job is still active on
             a live node; not transitioning to terminal."
             JobStatus=RUNNING DriverNodeID=1fdaa65c52efe92a...
[07:00:02Z] js=SUCCEEDED dep=Complete
```

**The #4091 case still fails, as it must.** Killing the head's `DashboardAgent` takes the node down: the entrypoint process dies and Ray's status freezes at `RUNNING`. The driver's node stops reporting `ALIVE`, so the timeout fires exactly as before.

```
[06:42:58Z] killed DashboardAgent   → node state=DEAD, entrypoint gone
[06:43:31Z] js=FAILED dep=Failed
            reason=JobDeploymentStatusTransitionGracePeriodExceeded
```

Force-deleting the head is also still terminal:

```
[06:39:09Z] dep=Failed reason=AppFailed
            "Submitter completed but Ray job not found in RayCluster."
```

```
=== RUN   TestCheckSubmitterFinishedTimeoutAndUpdateStatusIfNeeded
    --- PASS: .../submitter_still_running
    --- PASS: .../grace_period_not_yet_elapsed
```

title: [Feature] Support per-pod FQDNs & inject to Ray node ip
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Ray pods are only addressable by pod IP, which changes on every recreation. Also when using mTLS feature, when scale up a worker, we will need to update the certificate to include the worker pod IP. This PR adds `spec.podFQDN` to RayCluster, giving each pod a resolvable DNS name: `<hostname>.<cluster>-headless.<ns>.svc.<cluster-domain>`, and optionally inject this to Ray node's `--node-ip-address`.

Two modes:
- `DNSOnly` (default): create per-pod DNS records only (pod `hostname`/`subdomain` + the headless worker Service). Ray keeps registering with pod IPs; FQDNs are for external consumers.
- `RegisterAsNodeAddress`: additionally inject the FQDN as `--node-ip-address`, so Ray nodes register and address each other by DNS name. This enables static DNS-SAN certificates for mTLS instead of re-issuing certs on every pod IP change.

Notes:
- Make the field is immutable: existing pods are not updated in place, so mutation would leave nodes registered under mixed identities. For using RayCluster recreate upgrade strategy, it will only delete pods only, which will leave a orphan service. We can consider making it mutable with recreate upgrade strategy.
- Skips pods that already have a `subdomain` (e.g. TPU multi-host webhook).


Manual test:
- Tested `RegisterAsNodeAddress` mode: https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/pull/5191#issuecomment-5385690894

- Add tests
- Support with mTLS

title: [CI][Flaky] Retry helm-unittest plugin install in the Helm workflow
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

The Helm workflow installs helm-unittest on every PR before any chart tests run:
`helm plugin install https://github.com/helm-unittest/helm-unittest.git --version 0.8.1`
That step downloads the v0.8.1 linux-amd64 archive from GitHub Releases. The real file is about ~23.6MB and for some CI runs GitHub returns the truncated file (tens or hundreds of KB). This appears to be a truncated/incorrect download instead of the chart test failure. This is a flaky download, so unrelated PRs (i.e. #5313) could failed even when they never touch Helm charts.

And the install step currently runs once, the retry on the next attempt usually gets the full archive. So I decide to retry `helm plugin install` up to 3 times in `.github/workflows/helm.yaml`, uninstall a partial plugin between attempts, which matched`helm pull` in `install/prometheus/install.sh`.

**Frequency of this flake**

This is uncommon but recurring. I confirmed 4 Helm runs whose failed step was `Install Helm unittest plugin` (job-level, not just run duration):

| Actions Run | Date | Duration | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/actions/runs/35287899111 | 2026-09-17 | 22s | #5313 |
| https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/actions/runs/31058225411 | 2026-08-05 | 2m19s | #5093 |
| https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/actions/runs/30808579171 | 2026-08-03 | 18s | #5011 |
| https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/actions/runs/30250840003 | 2026-07-27 | 22s | #5038 |

That is about once every ~2 weeks recently. The pattern is consistent: one matrix job fails during plugin install (`checksum`), and `fail-fast` cancels the other two before any chart tests run. So it still blocks unrelated PRs.

I couldn't give a complete all-time count. GitHub has expired older logs, and for runs before ~June 2026 the job `steps` arrays are also empty. There are additional ~20s fail-fast Helm failures earlier that look like the same pattern, but those logs details are gone, so I cannot count it.

## Related issue number

Closes #5323

title: Add stale issue/PR bot workflow
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

We have old issues and PRs that would benefit from being automatically marked stale and closed after prolonged inactivity.

Adds `.github/workflows/stale.yaml` using [`actions/stale@v9`](https://github.com/actions/stale), the same action Ray currently uses for its own [stale PR workflow](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/master/.github/workflows/stale_pull_request.yaml).

Ray's *current* workflow only handles PRs (issues are explicitly disabled). Ray previously handled issues too, via a now-retired [`probot-stale` config](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/9f40d3eeac887f982bc9528fd3c4d536415a1a77/.github/stale.yml). This PR carries that historical issue policy forward on top of Ray's current PR policy:

- **Issues**: 120 days inactivity → marked `stale`; 14 more days → closed. Exempt labels: `P0`, `P0.5`, `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `good-first-issue`, `release-blocker`.
- **Pull requests**: 120 days inactivity → marked `stale`; 14 more days → closed. Exempt labels: `release-blocker`, `branch-cut-blocker`.

The day thresholds and exempt labels are easy to tune in a single place if maintainers prefer different values — flagging this explicitly since [a comment on #681](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/681#issuecomment-5078063424) noted the timeframe should be a maintainer decision.

## Related issue number

Closes #681

Full Changelog: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/compare/v0.25.0...v0.25.1

v0.25.0

Highlights

This version of controller-runtime introduces a new experimental ReadYourWritesConsistency feature, which ensures that all writes are reflected in subsequent reads from the default cache-backed client. Stale client reads are arguably the biggest source of friction and sometimes bugs for controller authors, providing this functionality at the library level eliminates that class of problems entirely.

Try it out by setting Client.EnableReadYourWritesConsistency: new(true) in your manager and leave any feedback you may have on the tracking issue.

body:
Bumps [google.golang.org/grpc](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go) from 1.82.1 to 1.83.2.
Release notes

Sourced from google.golang.org/grpc's releases.

Release 1.83.2

Security

  • server: Reject requests missing both :authority and Host headers with HTTP 400 and status Internal. (grpc/grpc-go#9365)
    • Special Thanks: @​winklemad

Release 1.83.1

Security

  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where nested Principal or Permission rules with :scheme or grpc- prefixed header matchers were not rejected, which could cause DENY rules to fail open. (#9258)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where the host header matcher was not being replaced with :authority in nested Principal or Permission rules. (#9258)
    • Special Thanks: @​nvxbug
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a header matcher whose name was not lowercase, such as X-Role, matched no header, which could cause DENY rules to fail open. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a :scheme or grpc- prefixed header matcher was accepted when its name was not lowercase. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony
  • xds/rbac: Fix a bug where a Host header matcher was not replaced with :authority. (#9332)
    • Special Thanks: @​alimony

Performance

  • transport: Restrict memory overhead of buffering small data frames. (#9331)

Release 1.83.0

Security

  • server: Stop reading from connections when flooded by HTTP/2 frames to mitigate resource exhaustion. The default value for this limit is 100 frames, excluding DATA and HEADERS, and may be changed by setting environment variable GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT.
  • xds/rbac: Support Metadata and RequestedServerName permissions matcher fields. If present in a DENY rule, previously these would be ignored and fail-open.
  • xds/rbac: Fix panic when parsing unsupported fields in NotRule/NotId permissions.
  • xds/rbac: Support the deprecated source_ip principal identifier by treating it as equivalent to direct_remote_ip.
  • xds: Fix panic when parsing route header matchers configured with empty exact_match, prefix_match, or suffix_match strings. (#9223)

New Features

  • xds/googlec2p: Enable DirectPath over Interconnect support for on-premises clients via the force-xds target URI query parameter. (#9133)
  • xds: Enable xDS configuration to control which fields get propagated from ORCA backend metric reports to LRS load reports. (#9145)
  • authz: Add OnPolicyUpdate callback to FileWatcherOptions to notify when an authz policy is loaded or updated. (#9142)
    • Special Thanks: @​hnefatl
  • xds: Add support for the GCP Authentication HTTP Filter, which automatically fetches and attaches GCP Service Account Identity JWT tokens to outgoing RPCs.
    • This feature can be enabled by setting environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_GCP_AUTHENTICATION_FILTER=true. (#9119)
  • xds: Add support for xDS-based HTTP CONNECT proxies.
    • This feature can be enabled by setting environment variable GRPC_EXPERIMENTAL_XDS_HTTP_CONNECT=true. (#9151)
  • xds: Add support for contains_match in route header matchers. (#9223)

Bug Fixes

  • credentials/alts: Fix panic when processing malformed frames by validating that the message frame length exceeds the message type field size. (#9197)
  • grpc: Fix compilation on Plan 9 targets (GOOS=plan9), broken since v1.81.0. (#9255)
    • Special Thanks: @​Yusufihsangorgel

Because RayClusterSpec defines 35 fields, but the Helm chart only renders 19 of them. This leaves `authOptions` and `upgradeStrategy`unavailable to users who install via Helm, even though both fields work out of the box on a standard KubeRay operator with no feature gate required.

title: ci: retry helm-unittest plugin install on transient download failure
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

The "Helm" CI workflow occasionally fails before any chart tests run, while
installing the `helm-unittest` plugin in `.github/workflows/helm.yaml`. GitHub
occasionally serves a truncated archive for the plugin release download, which
fails helm's checksum verification and fails the whole job for unrelated PRs
(not a real chart test failure).

## Related issue number

title: [kubectl-plugin] add "scale rayservice" command for end-to-end worker-group scaling
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`kubectl ray scale` currently supports only `scale cluster`, which updates a live RayCluster's worker-group bounds — a change that is lost when the cluster is replaced. Users of RayService have no first-class scaling command: a durable *and* effective scale change requires patching the RayService and the live RayCluster separately, by hand.

This PR adds `kubectl ray scale rayservice`:

```
kubectl ray scale rayservice my-service --worker-group my-group --min-replicas 2 --max-replicas 6
```

The command resolves the active RayCluster from `status.activeServiceStatus.rayClusterName` and updates the worker group's min/max replicas on both objects in one invocation:

- **RayService** `spec.rayClusterConfig.workerGroupSpecs[*]` — durable; the bounds survive cluster replacement
- **live RayCluster** `spec.workerGroupSpecs[*]` — takes effect immediately

Implementation details:

- **JSON patch** (`application/json-patch+json`) at `groupName`-resolved indices, with a `test` op on `resourceVersion` for optimistic concurrency. `add` ops are used because `minReplicas`/`maxReplicas` are optional (`omitempty`) fields that may be absent from the stored object. The `workerGroupSpecs` list is never merge-patched, since a merge patch on that array drops the required `template` field.
- **Refuses while an incremental upgrade is in progress** (`status.pendingServiceStatus.rayClusterName` set), since the patch target is ambiguous then.
- **Validates each object's final state** (min ≤ max after applying the flags to that object's current values), so a bound that is valid for the RayService but not for the live cluster fails before anything is written.
- **Idempotent on retry**: unchanged objects are skipped, so re-running the command after a partial failure applies only the missing write. If the live-cluster patch fails after the RayService was updated, the command explains that the bounds are recorded durably and will take effect when the cluster is next replaced.
- **`--replicas` is deliberately not offered**: for a RayService the replica count is managed by the Ray autoscaler, and min/max bounds are the user-facing knobs. `kubectl ray scale cluster` remains available for direct RayCluster replica control.

This implements item 2 of #5325, which maps the full layer picture behind this design.

title: raycluster: replace workers stuck terminating
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

When a worker pod is stuck Terminating, KubeRay still counts it toward the desired replica total. A worker group can remain below its requested active capacity until someone removes the terminating pod manually.

The reconciler excludes pods with a deletion timestamp from worker health checks and replica accounting, so it can replace the missing active worker while Kubernetes finishes deleting the old pod.

The sidecar end-to-end check also waits for cluster removal after job completion. These happen in separate reconciles; checking for immediate removal caused the CI failure shown below.

## Related issue number

Fixes https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/4078

Sidecar CI failure: https://buildkite.com/ray-project/ray-ecosystem-ci-kuberay-ci/builds/16976#01a08267-7e55-4167-9792-63b3eb08614c

## Labels

- [x] If this PR has user-facing changes that require documentation updates at release time, I have added the `doc-updates-required` label.
- [x] If this PR contains breaking changes, I have added the `breaking-change` label.

Neither conditional label applies to this bug fix.

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Manual tests
- [ ] This PR is not tested :(

## Testing Done

### Manual test instructions

| # | Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Replace a terminating worker | Patch and delete the live worker as shown below | Active workers change from zero to one while the old pod still exists. |
| 2 | Sidecar job completion followed by cluster cleanup | Run the selected sidecar test below | The immediate check fails; the waiting check passes. |

#### Worker replacement

The base controller at https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/commit/39b5d98d9ce99d7839d7c32b323e2d95f7257910 left the worker unreplaced after 30 seconds. Switching only the controller to https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/commit/073dbc5f670acb54309132c260104280d9c17b44 restored a Ready worker while the same old pod remained Terminating.

The workload was created by the real controller and reached Ready before deletion. A finalizer held the subsequent deletion to reproduce the stuck-Terminating state.

Use two checkouts to build the named controller versions:

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/kuberay-base 39b5d98d9ce99d7839d7c32b323e2d95f7257910
git worktree add /tmp/kuberay-fixed 073dbc5f670acb54309132c260104280d9c17b44
(cd /tmp/kuberay-base/ray-operator && go build -o /tmp/operator-base main.go)
(cd /tmp/kuberay-fixed/ray-operator && go build -o /tmp/operator-fixed main.go)
```

Start the base controller against a local kind cluster with the repository CRDs installed:

```bash
/tmp/operator-base -leader-election-namespace default -use-kubernetes-proxy
```

Apply this workload, using the verified Ray 2.55.0 image already loaded into kind:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: kuberay-worker-proof
---
apiVersion: ray.io/v1
kind: RayCluster
metadata:
  name: terminating-worker-live
  namespace: kuberay-worker-proof
spec:
  rayVersion: "2.55.0"
  headGroupSpec:
    rayStartParams: {dashboard-host: "0.0.0.0", num-cpus: "1"}
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
          - name: ray-head
            image: rayproject/ray:2.55.0
            imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
            env: [{name: RAY_USAGE_STATS_ENABLED, value: "0"}]
            resources:
              requests: {cpu: 300m, memory: 1G}
              limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 8G}
  workerGroupSpecs:
    - groupName: workers
      replicas: 1
      minReplicas: 1
      maxReplicas: 1
      rayStartParams: {num-cpus: "1"}
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: ray-worker
              image: rayproject/ray:2.55.0
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              env: [{name: RAY_USAGE_STATS_ENABLED, value: "0"}]
              resources:
                requests: {cpu: 300m, memory: 1G}
                limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 4G}
```

```bash
NS=kuberay-worker-proof
CLUSTER=terminating-worker-live
kubectl wait raycluster/"$CLUSTER" -n "$NS" \
  --for=jsonpath='{.status.state}'=ready --timeout=300s
kubectl wait pod -n "$NS" -l "ray.io/cluster=$CLUSTER" \
  --for=condition=Ready --timeout=120s
WORKER=$(kubectl get pod -n "$NS" \
  -l "ray.io/cluster=$CLUSTER,ray.io/node-type=worker" \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl patch pod -n "$NS" "$WORKER" --type=merge \
  -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":["test.kuberay.io/hold"]}}'
kubectl delete pod -n "$NS" "$WORKER" --wait=false
sleep 30
kubectl get pods -n "$NS" -l "ray.io/cluster=$CLUSTER" \
  -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.metadata.labels.ray\.io/node-type,PHASE:.status.phase,DELETING:.metadata.deletionTimestamp' \
  --no-headers
kubectl get pods -n "$NS" \
  -l "ray.io/cluster=$CLUSTER,ray.io/node-type=worker" -o json |
  jq -r '"ACTIVE_WORKERS=\([.items[] | select(.metadata.deletionTimestamp == null)] | length)\nTOTAL_WORKERS=\(.items | length)"'
```

Base controller, after the 30-second observation:

```text
controller_ref=39b5d98d9ce99d7839d7c32b323e2d95f7257910
wait_seconds=30
ACTIVE_WORKERS=0
TOTAL_WORKERS=1
```

Stop that controller and start the fixed controller against the same cluster and unchanged workload:

```bash
/tmp/operator-fixed -leader-election-namespace default -use-kubernetes-proxy
```

Wait for the replacement, then repeat the pod-count command:

```bash
kubectl wait raycluster/terminating-worker-live -n kuberay-worker-proof \
  --for=jsonpath='{.status.readyWorkerReplicas}'=1 --timeout=180s
```

Fixed controller:

```text
controller_ref=073dbc5f670acb54309132c260104280d9c17b44
ACTIVE_WORKERS=1
TOTAL_WORKERS=2
```

<details>
<summary>Raw worker replacement logs</summary>

Before:

```text
terminating-worker-live-workers-worker-kr4js   Failed    2026-09-19T21:47:34Z
ACTIVE_WORKERS=0
TOTAL_WORKERS=1
```

After:

```text
terminating-worker-live-workers-worker-kr4js   Failed    2026-09-19T21:47:34Z
terminating-worker-live-workers-worker-t8kg6   Running   active
ACTIVE_WORKERS=1
TOTAL_WORKERS=2
```

The test finalizer keeps the original pod present during the observation.

</details>

#### Sidecar cleanup

Both runs used the same current-master operator binary, a real kind Kubernetes 1.29 cluster, and Ray 2.55.0. The test file on this branch is byte-identical to the file exercised. The controller's supported request-rate settings expose the gap between completing a job and deleting its cluster; no resource status was fabricated.

The local ARM64 head needed an 8G memory limit to start Ray. The same allowance was applied in both runs; Ray's memory-protection settings were not changed.

From the operator directory, start the controller in one shell:

```bash
go build -o /tmp/kuberay-manager main.go
/tmp/kuberay-manager -leader-election-namespace default \
  -use-kubernetes-proxy -metrics-addr=127.0.0.1:18862 \
  -health-probe-bind-address=127.0.0.1:18863 -qps=0.5 -burst=1
```

The original assertion comes from the base checkout above. The corrected test file comes from the final test commit; it is byte-identical to the one exercised on the base snapshot. Build both test versions explicitly:

```bash
(cd /tmp/kuberay-base/ray-operator && go test -p 2 -c -o /tmp/sidecar-before ./test/e2erayjob)
git show a400496796b391a8d5de0993522b9386900888cd:ray-operator/test/e2erayjob/rayjob_sidecar_mode_test.go \
  > /tmp/kuberay-base/ray-operator/test/e2erayjob/rayjob_sidecar_mode_test.go
(cd /tmp/kuberay-base/ray-operator && go test -p 2 -c -o /tmp/sidecar-after ./test/e2erayjob)
```

Run once with the original test and once with the corrected test, using the same controller setup. Local binary paths are shortened here:

```bash
TEST_BINARY=/tmp/sidecar-before
# Use /tmp/sidecar-after for the second run.
KUBERAY_TEST_RAY_IMAGE=rayproject/ray:2.55.0 \
KUBERAY_TEST_RAY_VERSION=2.55.0 \
KUBERAY_TEST_TIMEOUT_MEDIUM=5m \
GOMAXPROCS=2 "$TEST_BINARY" -test.v \
  -test.run '^TestRayJobSidecarMode$/^Successful_RayJob$' \
  -test.count=1 -test.timeout=10m
```

Once the test logs that it created the RayJob, apply the local ARM64 allowance in a third shell:

```bash
NS=$(kubectl get rayjobs -A -o json |
  jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name=="counter") | .metadata.namespace')
kubectl wait -n "$NS" rayjob/counter \
  --for=jsonpath='{.status.rayClusterName}' --timeout=120s
RC=$(kubectl get rayjob counter -n "$NS" -o jsonpath='{.status.rayClusterName}')
kubectl patch raycluster "$RC" -n "$NS" --type=json \
  -p '[{"op":"test","path":"/spec/headGroupSpec/template/spec/containers/0/name","value":"ray-head"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/headGroupSpec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"8G"}]'
```

Selected controller-log fields show the real lifecycle gap. In the before run, the job became Complete at 13:22:00.112, but cluster deletion happened at 13:22:02.101. The immediate assertion had already failed and begun cleanup at 13:22:01.

```json
{"ts":"2026-09-19T13:22:00.112-0700","msg":"updateRayJobStatus","jobStatus":"SUCCEEDED","jobDeploymentStatus":"Complete","rayClusterName":"counter-f4qc6"}
{"ts":"2026-09-19T13:22:02.101-0700","msg":"The associated RayCluster for RayJob is deleted"}
{"ts":"2026-09-19T13:22:02.102-0700","msg":"The associated RayCluster for RayJob has been already deleted and it can not be found"}
```

Before, on the original assertion:

```text
    rayjob_sidecar_mode_test.go:82:
        Expected
            <bool>: false
        to be true
--- FAIL: TestRayJobSidecarMode (90.55s)
    --- FAIL: TestRayJobSidecarMode/Successful_RayJob (90.49s)
FAIL
exit_code=1
```

After, the controller still completed the job before removing its cluster:

```json
{"ts":"2026-09-19T15:08:43.364-0700","msg":"updateRayJobStatus","jobStatus":"SUCCEEDED","jobDeploymentStatus":"Complete","rayClusterName":"counter-bnm64"}
{"ts":"2026-09-19T15:08:45.359-0700","msg":"The associated RayCluster for RayJob is deleted"}
{"ts":"2026-09-19T15:08:45.360-0700","msg":"The associated RayCluster for RayJob has been already deleted and it can not be found"}
```

The corrected check then recorded its own observation, after its API query returned NotFound:

```text
rayjob_sidecar_mode_test.go:83: [2026-09-19T15:08:46-07:00] RayCluster test-ns-bnfzl/counter-bnm64 is no longer present
exit_code=0
```

title: fix: use resolved config for log encoders when --config file is set
body:
## What I did

When `--config` is used, `logStdoutEncoder` and `logFileEncoder` are loaded into the configuration, but `main.go` still built the zap encoders from the raw flag variables. The flag defaults ("json") therefore silently overrode the file values — while the flag help text says "Flags are ignored if config file is set".

- Use `config.LogStdoutEncoder` / `config.LogFileEncoder` when creating the encoders (as suggested in the issue).
- Without a config file, behavior is unchanged: the else branch copies the flag values into `config`, so both code paths read the same values.
- `newLogEncoder` treats an empty value as json, matching the flag default, so a config file that omits the encoder fields still gets json.

Verification: `go build ./...` and `go vet` pass in ray-operator.

Fixes #5309

title: [History Server] Add OCI Object Storage backend
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

The history server and collector support S3/MinIO, GCS, Azure Blob and Aliyun OSS. This adds Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Object Storage as `--storage-backend=oci`, so KubeRay clusters on OKE (or anywhere with OCI credentials) can store and browse Ray session history without going through the S3-compatibility endpoint.

- New `historyserver/pkg/storage/oci` implementing `StorageWriter`/`StorageReader` on the OCI Go SDK (`objectstorage`), registered in the collector registry and listed in the `--storage-backend` flag help.
- Configuration via `OCI_BUCKET`, `OCI_NAMESPACE` (resolved with `GetNamespace` when empty), `OCI_REGION`, `OCI_COMPARTMENT_ID` (enables bucket auto-create), `OCI_AUTH_TYPE`, `OCI_CONFIG_FILE`, `OCI_CONFIG_PROFILE`, or the matching `oci*` keys of the backend JSON file (env first, JSON wins, same as azureblob).
- Auth: `api_key`, `session_token`, `instance_principal`, `oke_workload_identity`, `resource_principal`, with auto-detection (Workload Identity inside OKE pods, the OCI config file locally, instance principal otherwise). An invalid explicit value fails at construction.
- Same object layout and semantics as the other backends: zero-byte `<dir>/` markers, paginated listing via `NextStartWith` with markers filtered out of `ListFiles`, `GetContent` falling back to a recursive listing of the parent directory (as s3/aliyunoss do), SDK default retry policy on every request, and a longer HTTP client timeout so large log downloads do not hit the SDK's 60s default. Leading `/` is trimmed from object names on both read and write so keys are Console-friendly.
- Bucket bootstrap: `HeadBucket`; on 404 the bucket is created if `OCI_COMPARTMENT_ID` is set (409 treated as success), otherwise a clear error notes that OCI returns 404 for both "missing" and "not permitted".
- Samples `config/rayjob-oci.yaml` and `config/historyserver-oci.yaml` (OKE Workload Identity) and docs updates.
- No `ray-operator` changes: the collector env validation intentionally skips unknown backends, and OCI has no strictly-required env var (bucket defaults, namespace and region are resolvable).

Dependency: `github.com/oracle/oci-go-sdk/v65` plus three small indirect modules, added with `go get` + `go mod tidy` the same way the Aliyun SDK was.

## Related issue number

N/A

## Labels

- [x] If this PR has user-facing changes that require documentation updates at release time, I have added the `doc-updates-required` label. (I cannot set labels on this repo; please add it.)
- [ ] If this PR contains breaking changes, I have added the `breaking-change` label.

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
  - [x] Unit tests
  - [x] Manual tests

Static: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint fmt` clean; `golangci-lint run -c ../.golangci.yml ./pkg/storage/oci/...` reports 0 issues. `go test -race ./pkg/... ./cmd/... -parallel 4` (the repo's `make test`) passes for all 14 packages, including 34 new tests in `pkg/storage/oci` driven through an in-memory fake of the Object Storage client (round-trips, pagination with page size 2, marker filtering, `List` sort/decoding including RayJob/RayService owners, `GetContent` direct/fallback/miss/non-404, namespace resolution, bucket create/conflict/missing-without-compartment, env/JSON config precedence, auth parsing and auto-detect matrix, provider construction).

### Manual test instructions

1. Create a bucket, or set `OCI_COMPARTMENT_ID` so the backend creates it. Authenticate with `oci session authenticate` locally, or use Workload Identity on OKE (`OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_VERSION=2.2` and `OCI_RESOURCE_PRINCIPAL_REGION`, as set in the samples).
2. Run the collector and history server with `STORAGE_BACKEND=oci`, `OCI_BUCKET`, `OCI_REGION`, and optionally `OCI_AUTH_TYPE` / `OCI_CONFIG_PROFILE`.
3. Open the history server, pick the stored session, and browse its logs.

What was run against a real OCI tenancy (us-ashburn-1, session-token auth, throwaway buckets deleted afterwards):

- Writer through the exported `NewWriter`: `CreateDirectory` (idempotent on re-run, no second PUT), `WriteFile` for the metadata marker, a 115 B file, a 30 KB file and a nested `logs/events/` file, using the collector's real key layout.
- Reader through `NewReader`: `List()` decodes exactly the one stored session; `ListFiles` returns base names plus `subdir/` with markers filtered; `GetContent` direct, 30 KB, listing fallback (asked for `event_RAYLET.log` at `logs/`, served from `logs/events/`), and a miss returning nil.

title: fix(dashboard): add missing kind segment to enter_cluster URL
body:
## Summary
`dashboard/src/hooks/api/useHistoryClusters.ts:27` built `/enter_cluster/{namespace}/{cluster}/{session}`, but since #4918 the history server route is `/enter_cluster/{namespace}/{kind}/{name}/{session}` (`historyserver/pkg/historyserver/router.go:385`). The 3-segment form the hook sent instead matches the "session defaults to latest" route (`router.go:373`), so the cluster name landed in `{kind}` and got rejected:

```
400 unsupported resource kind: "raycluster-historyserver"
```

No cluster cookie is set in that case, so every following cluster-scoped call returns "Cluster Cookie not found". The History tab lists sessions fine, but Tasks and Logs stay permanently empty.

## Fix
Insert the missing `kind` segment. Every entry returned by `GET /clusters` represents a RayCluster resource — the response's `OwnerKind`/`OwnerName` (`historyserver/pkg/utils/types.go`) describe the RayJob/RayService that *owns* the cluster, not the kind of the list entry itself — so the segment is always `"raycluster"`, matching `utils.RayClusterKind` on the backend (`historyserver/pkg/utils/constant.go:15`).

Fixes #5172

## Test plan
- [x] `npx eslint src/hooks/api/useHistoryClusters.ts` and `npx prettier --check` clean
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors from this change (the 5 pre-existing errors are unrelated missing static-asset imports from a sparse checkout, not from this file)
- [ ] Manual repro from the issue (`curl .../enter_cluster/default/raycluster-historyserver/$SESSION` → 200, matching the reported fix) — could not run the full historyserver + kind cluster setup in this environment

title: K8sJobMode: Honour Ray address overrides in submitter health checks
body:
## Why are these changes needed 

KubeRay 1.7.0 added [a dashboard health check](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/blob/v1.7.0/ray-operator/controllers/ray/common/job.go#L132-L151) to the default K8sJobMode submitter. The check probes the generated Kubernetes service address directly (coreDNS), rather than going through the `RAY_ADDRESS` env var address resolution, which is what job submission itself uses.

That difference matters in clusters with custom DNS or service discovery (many large enterprises have this constraint like where I work: Stripe), where the generated coreDNS service address isn't reachable. Until 1.7.0, this was not an issue as Ray's submission client honoured the `RAY_ADDRESS` env var. However, the new health check does not. As a result, the submitter blocks on the probe and never reaches `ray job submit`, even though the dashboard is reachable at the configured `RAY_ADDRESS` env var.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the health-check address inside the submitter mimicking the env var resolution from  get_address_for_submission_client(). The probe follows RAY_API_SERVER_ADDRESS/RAY_ADDRESS precedence where that's supported, so the check and the submission always target the same endpoint.

The change applies only to K8sJobMode. SidecarMode retains its existing localhost health check.

## Related issue number

https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/issues/5282

title: [History Server] Cache JSON bytes and share the decoded snapshot via a weak pointer
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Based on the comment https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/pull/5208#discussion_r3969000721, storing the Go struct directly is not a good choice, as there's no way for us to accurately estimate Go struct memory usage, and a fixed factor is not ideal.

This PR follows the method mentioned in https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/pull/5208#discussion_r3969000721: it still stores the encoded JSON bytes in the LRU cache, alongside a weak pointer which points to the decoded snapshot, so concurrent requests can share the same decoded object rather than each request holding a separate copy. The byte budget goes back to counting the exact JSON length, so the 2.5x heap factor from #5208 is removed.

title: fix(historyserver): discover node ID locally instead of querying the dashboard
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

The history collector discovers its Ray node ID by calling `GET /api/v0/nodes?limit=10000` against the head dashboard: once at startup (12 retries, fatal on failure), then every 5 seconds from both the event and log collector tickers. Each call makes StateHead aggregate and serialize the full node table, so load grows with the square of cluster size.

We hit this in production on a 256-worker cluster: it produced roughly 100 full-table requests per second sustained, drove StateHead to a permanent ~50% CPU burn, and eventually wedged it. The startup retry herd from crashlooping workers then kept it down.

## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

Discover the node ID locally instead of over the network:

- Read `{RAY_TMP_ROOT}/raylet_node_id`, which a lifecycle hook on the Ray container publishes by inspecting its own raylet process (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, matched to the current session). Zero network calls in both the startup and ticker paths. The file is authoritative for the container's lifetime; in-process Ray restarts that rotate the node ID are out of scope, matching the publisher's container-restart granularity.
- Keep the dashboard query as a fallback for deployments without a publisher, but harden it for scale:
  - server-side filtering (`node_ip` and `state=ALIVE`) replaces the full-table `limit=10000` fetch
  - the 1s client timeout, which guaranteed failure on a busy dashboard, is raised to 10s
  - the fixed 5s retry interval gains jitter so a fleet of starting workers doesn't retry in phase-locked waves

## Related issue number

None filed yet — happy to open one if maintainers want a tracking issue before/alongside this PR.

title: [History Server] Fix live pass-through across namespaces
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Live pass-through previously built its direct target from the head Service short
name (`http://<service>:<port>`). Kubernetes only resolves that name within the
caller's namespace, so a History Server running separately from its Ray clusters
received 502 responses when proxying live Dashboard requests.

The existing `--use-kubernetes-proxy` alternative carries the namespace in the
API server proxy URL, but the History Server ClusterRole did not grant
`services/proxy`. Enabling the flag therefore replaced the DNS failure with a
403 response.

This PR fixes both paths:

- use the namespace-qualified Service DNS name
  (`<service>.<namespace>.svc`) for direct in-cluster connections; this works
  across namespaces without assuming a particular cluster domain
- add the `services/proxy` permission required by the optional Kubernetes API
  proxy path
- document `--use-kubernetes-proxy` as an opt-in in all three History Server
  sample manifests

The Kubernetes API proxy path was verified in-cluster:

1. Deploy the History Server in namespace `kuberay-system` and a RayCluster in a

against a live cluster as part of this PR update.

title: [RayCluster][Kueue] Delete Services during suspension
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

Suspending a RayCluster deleted its Pods but left the head, serve, and headless Services behind. This made standalone RayCluster inconsistent with the other suspend paths.

This PR deletes those Services while suspended and recreates them on resume. It preserves the existing suspend commit point, but tears Pods down before Services so a failed Service deletion cannot block quota release.

The status path now tolerates the head Service being absent during suspension, allowing the suspend/resume transition to complete normally.

Scope is limited to the Pods and Services called out in #4876. Other owned resources have different lifecycle semantics and are left unchanged.

One behavior worth calling out: `RayClusterSuspended` still becomes true once the Pods are gone, rather than waiting for every owned resource to be deleted.

## Related issue number

title: [history server][collector] Migrate to new AWS S3 SDK version
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

### Summary
This PR migrates the historyserver S3 integration from AWS SDK for Go v1 to v2 to address the deprecation of the v1 SDK.

The scope is intentionally kept focused on the SDK migration itself, plus the minimal MinIO endpoint compatibility update needed for the v2 S3 client configuration used in historyserver e2e manifests.

## Changes

- migrate historyserver S3 client initialization from AWS SDK v1 to v2
- replace v1 pagination with AWS SDK v2 paginators
- replace v1 AWS error handling with v2-compatible error handling
- update historyserver e2e S3 test client/helpers to AWS SDK v2

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?
Second PR of the series adding device-agnostic node label delivery webhook. #5260 added the `topology.labelMappings` field and the `allowedNodeLabels` operator config. This PR adds the verification step checking for valid topology group before the delivery.

The rules being enforced by `validateTopology`, which is called by the validating webhooks, are the following:
- every `nodeLabel` must be in the `allowedNodeLabels`
- there can't be duplicate ray label keys from mapping
- `ray.io/overwrite-container-cmd` shouldn't be set
- users shouldn't run `ray start` in their container command

If any of these are not honored, the API server rejects with an error that specifies the culprit field, so that the users could see the reason in the `kubectl apply` output.

A group with no `topology` or an empty `labelMappings` (with topology field set) results in a no-op.

body:

<!-- Please add a reviewer to the assignee section when you create a PR. If you don't have the access to it, we will shortly find a reviewer and assign them to your PR. -->

## Why are these changes needed?

Third PR of the series adding device-agnostic node label delivery webhook, stacked on #5298. 

Adds the `pods CREATE` mutating webhook. When the `TopologyLabelDelivery` gate is on and a Ray worker pod's group sets `topology.labelMappings`, it:
1. adds a downward API env var `RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON` pointing at the pod's `ray.io/topology-labels` annotation
2. rewrites the args so the KubeRay-generated `ray start` writes that value to `/tmp/ray-labels.yaml` and runs with `--labels-file`.

The annotation is written at bind time by the binding webhook in 4/n.
<!-- Please give a short summary of the change and the problem this solves. -->

## Related issue number

<!-- For example: "Closes #1234" -->

## Labels

<!-- Please add the appropriate labels to this PR. -->

- [x] If this PR has user-facing changes that require documentation updates at release time, I have added the `doc-updates-required` label.
- [ ] If this PR contains breaking changes, I have added the `breaking-change` label.

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
  - [x] Unit tests
  - [x] Manual tests
  - [ ] This PR is not tested :(

<!-- If you selected "Manual tests" above, please fill in the section below. Otherwise you can remove it. -->

### Manual test instructions

TLDR: on a kind cluster, deployed the operator with the webhook and confirmed that:
1) a worker pod with the `topolgy.labelMappings` is mutated at CREATE
2) pods outside that scope are untouched
3) the feature gate behaved as designed.

#### Verifies the following expected behaviors

- Gate off: a RayCluster with `topology.labelMappings` is rejected at reconcile and no pod is created.
- Gate on:  a topology worker gets the `RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON` downward API env var and `--labels-file` in its `ray start` args
- Worker groups that do not opt in through `topology.labelMappings` are left unchanged.
- Non-Ray pods are admitted without triggering the webhook

<!--
  Provide step-by-step instructions so reviewers can verify your changes.
  Include any relevant screenshots or logs demonstrating the behavior.
-->

Prerequisites: kind, kubectl, docker. Node labels are not needed for this PR; nothing reads them at CREATE.

**1. Cluster, cert-manager, operator image**

```bash
kind create cluster --name tas
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.17.2/cert-manager.yaml
kubectl -n cert-manager wait deploy --all --for=condition=Available --timeout=180s
cd ray-operator
make docker-image IMG=kuberay/operator:pr3
kind load docker-image kuberay/operator:pr3 --name tas
```

**2. Deploy the operator with webhooks, then switch it to a config file carrying the allowlist. Gate stays off for now.**

```bash
kubectl kustomize config/default-with-webhooks | sed 's#quay.io/kuberay/operator:nightly#kuberay/operator:pr3#' | kubectl apply --server-side -f -
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: kuberay-operator-config, namespace: ray-system}
data:
  config.yaml: |
    apiVersion: config.ray.io/v1alpha1
    kind: Configuration
    allowedNodeLabels: [topology.kubernetes.io/zone, nvidia.com/gpu.cliuqe]
EOF
kubectl -n ray-system patch deploy kuberay-operator --type strategic -p '
spec: {template: {spec: {containers: [{name: kuberay-operator, args: [--config=/etc/kuberay/config.yaml],
  volumeMounts: [{name: operator-config, mountPath: /etc/kuberay, readOnly: true}]}],
  volumes: [{name: operator-config, configMap: {name: kuberay-operator-config}}]}}}'
kubectl -n ray-system rollout status deploy/kuberay-operator
kubectl -n ray-system logs deploy/kuberay-operator | grep "Loaded feature gates"   # TopologyLabelDelivery:false
```

**3. Gate off: a topology RayCluster is rejected before any pod exists.**

```bash
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: ray.io/v1
kind: RayCluster
metadata: {name: topo}
spec:
  headGroupSpec:
    rayStartParams: {dashboard-host: "0.0.0.0"}
    template: {spec: {containers: [{name: ray-head, image: rayproject/ray:2.49.0}]}}
  workerGroupSpecs:
  - groupName: plain
    replicas: 1
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 1
    template: {spec: {containers: [{name: ray-worker, image: rayproject/ray:2.49.0}]}}
  - groupName: topo
    replicas: 1
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 1
    topology: {labelMappings: [{nodeLabel: nvidia.com/gpu.clique, mapTo: ray.io/gpu-domain}, {nodeLabel: topology.kubernetes.io/zone}]}
    template: {spec: {containers: [{name: ray-worker, image: rayproject/ray:2.49.0}]}}
EOF
sleep 10; kubectl get pods            # none
kubectl get events --field-selector reason=InvalidRayClusterSpec
# ... worker group topo sets topology, which requires the TopologyLabelDelivery feature gate to be enabled
```

**4. Gate on: pods are created and the topology worker is mutated at CREATE.**

```bash
kubectl -n ray-system patch deploy kuberay-operator --type json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-","value":"--feature-gates=TopologyLabelDelivery=true"}]'
kubectl -n ray-system rollout status deploy/kuberay-operator
kubectl wait pod -l ray.io/node-type=head --for=condition=Ready --timeout=300s
T=$(kubectl get pod -l ray.io/group=topo -o name); P=$(kubectl get pod -l ray.io/group=plain -o name)

kubectl get $T -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON")]}{"\n"}'
#  {"name":"RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON","valueFrom":{"fieldRef":{"fieldPath":"metadata.annotations['ray.io/topology-labels']"}}}
kubectl get $T -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].args[0]}{"\n"}' | grep -o --'--labels-file=[^ ]*'
#  --labels-file=/tmp/ray-labels.yaml
kubectl get $T -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.ray\.io/topology-labels}{"\n"}'   # empty
sleep 60; kubectl get $T       # CrashLoopBackOff
kubectl logs $T -c ray-worker --previous | tail -1
#  RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON is empty: node labels were not delivered to this pod,see the pod events

kubectl get $P -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].env[*].name}{"\n"}'   # no RAY_NODE_LABELS_JSON
kubectl get $P                                                          # Running
```

**5. Non-Ray pods bypass the fail-closed webhook.**

```bash
kubectl run nginx --image=nginx --restart=Never
kubectl wait pod/nginx --for=condition=Ready --timeout=60s
```

title: [ray-operator] Add noDriverTimeoutSeconds for idle RayCluster termination
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

## Why are these changes needed?

Related to https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/63465

This PR adds the KubeRay operator side of cluster-level idle termination driven by the v2 Ray autoscaler:

- Add `spec.autoscalerOptions.noDriverTimeoutSeconds`. The v2 autoscaler reads it and, once no user driver has been attached for that long, sets the `ray.io/no-driver-ttl-expired annotation` on the RayCluster.

title: [History Server] Cover GetContent object paths for the s3 and azureblob backends
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`GetContent` builds its object path from three pieces, `rootDir`, the cluster path prefix, and the file name. Neither the s3 nor the azureblob backend had a single test touching that. `pkg/storage/s3/s3_test.go` and `pkg/storage/azureblob/azureblob_test.go` contained only `TestTrim` and `TestWalk`, which never construct a handler, never call a storage method, and contain no assertion that can fail.

This is not a hypothetical gap. The aliyunoss backend shipped without the root dir in that path, which is #4820: on a deployment started with `--ray-root-dir`, listing the log tree worked and every fetch from it returned `NoSuchKey`. The same mistake in s3 or azureblob would produce the same silent breakage, and nothing in the suite would notice.

This PR adds two tests per backend. There is no production change.

## How the tests work

Each test drives the real SDK against an `httptest` server, so the assertion is on the object path that actually reaches the wire rather than on a helper's return value. For s3 that means path style addressing, which the backend already supports for MinIO. For azureblob the container client is pointed at the test server with no credential.

The first test in each pair pins the full object path. The second covers the list-and-retry fallback, whose listing prefix has to be rooted as well, otherwise the retry has nothing to find.

The two backends need slightly different fallback setups because their matching rules differ. s3 matches a listed candidate by base name, so the test puts the object one directory deeper. azureblob matches on the full path, so its test misses the first download instead. That one uses `BlobNotFound` rather than a server error on purpose: the SDK retries server errors, which would satisfy the download before the fallback ever ran.

## Related issue number

None. The gap was found while investigating #4820. It is not part of the #5065 follow-up epic, whose six items are all something else.

## Labels

- [ ] If this PR has user-facing changes that require documentation updates at release time, I have added the `doc-updates-required` label.
- [ ] If this PR contains breaking changes, I have added the `breaking-change` label.

## Checks

- [x] I've made sure the tests are passing.
- Testing Strategy
  - [x] Unit tests

### Evidence

New tests pass on both backends:

```
$ go test ./pkg/storage/s3/ ./pkg/storage/azureblob/ -run TestGetContent -v -count=1
=== RUN   TestGetContentUsesRootDir
--- PASS: TestGetContentUsesRootDir (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestGetContentFallbackListsUnderRootDir
--- PASS: TestGetContentFallbackListsUnderRootDir (0.00s)
ok  	.../pkg/storage/s3
ok  	.../pkg/storage/azureblob
```

A passing test against already correct code proves nothing on its own, so both backends were mutation tested. The production file was swapped in via `go test -overlay`, leaving the tree untouched.

**Mutation A, drop the root dir and cluster prefix from the object path.** Both tests go red on both backends:

```
--- FAIL: TestGetContentUsesRootDir
    s3_test.go:147: GetContent returned nil; keys requested:
      [session_2026-05-08.../event_CORE_WORKER_256.log],
      want "ray-logs/ray_cluster_history/raycluster/default/my-cluster/session_.../event_CORE_WORKER_256.log"
--- FAIL: TestGetContentFallbackListsUnderRootDir
```

**Mutation B, leave the object path correct and break only the fallback listing prefix.** Only the fallback test goes red, on both backends:

```
--- FAIL: TestGetContentFallbackListsUnderRootDir
    s3_test.go:195: GetContent returned nil; list prefixes tried:
      [ray_cluster_history/raycluster/default/my-cluster/session_.../events/]
```

Mutation B is the useful one: it shows the two tests in each pair are not redundant, since the second catches a defect the first cannot see.

**Rest of the module.** `go vet ./...` is clean and every non e2e package passes. The one failure, `TestGetSessionDir_FatalError_FailsFast` in `pkg/utils`, fails identically on a clean `origin/master` checkout on this machine and is unrelated to this change: it depends on symlink behavior this Windows host does not provide.

### What was not tested

- **Listing semantics.** The fake responses ignore the `delimiter` parameter, so flat versus hierarchical listing is not covered. Changing the s3 fallback from `_listFiles(dirPath, "", false)` to `_listFiles(dirPath, "/", false)` still passes. These tests are scoped to the object path, not to listing behavior.
- `go test -race`, which `make test` runs in CI, needs a C toolchain this machine does not have. Shared state in the tests is behind a mutex, since the servers handle requests on their own goroutines.
- No run against real S3, MinIO, or Azure Blob. These tests deliberately assert on the emitted object path, not on storage behavior.

---

_This change was developed with AI assistance from Claude. I reviewed and verified it before submitting._

title: rayservice: deduplicate target capacity updates using cluster status
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

During incremental RayService upgrades, capacity update deduplication reads `target_capacity` from the cached Serve config. That cache retains the original spec rather than the capacity most recently applied to the cluster. Comparing the original value with the next goal can skip a required Dashboard update and leave the upgrade stalled. For example, an active cluster at 80% that must scale down to 60% never advances if the original config also contains 60%.

Use the matching active or pending cluster's `Status.TargetCapacity` to identify an already-applied target. Missing status remains unknown and requires an update. Keep the original Serve config cache unchanged, and update capacity status only after `UpdateDeployments` succeeds. Reconciliation uses local defaults for missing capacities without recording those defaults as successful updates.

The regression reproduces a return to the original configured capacity through `reconcileServeTargetCapacity`, with and without a cached config. It also verifies that Dashboard failures preserve status and that retries apply the update. Additional tests cover active/pending status selection, missing status, repeated updates, and rollback with missing capacity status.

title: fix(rayjob): stop observed jobs after deadline expiry
body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`activeDeadlineSeconds` can mark a RayJob deployment as `Failed` while the Ray execution continues and `jobStatus` stays `RUNNING`.

For executions already observed as `PENDING` or `RUNNING`, this requests cancellation after `DeadlineExceeded` and polls until Ray reports a terminal status. It preserves the original deadline timestamp and failure count, keeps configured cleanup working, and does not delete shared clusters. A missing dashboard record preserves the last runtime status and stops cancellation polling; it does not confirm that the job stopped.
